name: Obagi Blue Peel

lead: The Obagi Blue Peel is a branded TCA-based medium peel. A 1999 paper described it as a standardized method with depth control.
Few studies exist beyond that and a hand-rejuvenation comparison.

paras: TCA causes controlled injury to the epidermis and upper dermis, after which skin sheds and renews.
Medium peels carry risks of pigment change, prolonged redness and scarring.

lead: The Obagi Blue Peel is a branded TCA-based medium-depth chemical peel. A 1999 Dermatologic Surgery paper described a standardized TCA-based blue peel intended to be deeper than superficial exfoliating peels while offering depth control, addressing the observation that TCA peel results vary with technique and patient selection.[1]

Published studies are few: a 2002 comparison of Er:YAG laser and Blue Peel for photoaged hands,[2] a 2006 paper on performing the peel faster and less expensively,[3] and a 2000 letter commenting on the technique.[4]

paras: The 1999 paper described a procedure using TCA at concentrations within the 30 to 50 percent range typical of TCA peels, with a modification intended to standardize penetration.[1] TCA peels in general are described as medium-depth, with warmth or burning during application and risks of pigment change and scarring.[5]

The 1999 report presented a standardized procedure rather than a controlled trial.[1] A 2002 study compared Er:YAG laser with Blue Peel in photoaged hands.[2] No large randomized trials of the Blue Peel for the face were found.

timeline.event: TCA-based blue peel standardized procedure published.[1]
